Ep. 1: director Daisuke Nishio, animation supervisor Masayuki Uchiyama, aired 26 Apr 1989. Ep. 2: director Osamu Kasai, animation supervisor Katsumi Aoshima, aired 3 May 1989. Ep. 2's anime-only verdict: 'nothing notable, aside from general padding'. Both compress into Kai ep. 1.
Ep. 2's working title was 'Father Son Goku's Past'; the auctioned script lists Piccolo in the cast as Ma Junior.

W-11 reports 18 May, Age 757 for Gohan’s birth; W-12 reports 28 November, Age 761 for Raditz’s arrival, yielding age four. The project’s separate guidebook chronology selects 12 October for Raditz (C067). These are competing secondary chronology accounts, not dialogue, and are not simultaneously settled.
No parent of Goku's is named anywhere in episode 2 — only "our father and mother". Bardock and Gine are named elsewhere in the franchise and not here (CC 00:20:50).

facts.statement: Ep. 3, at home (14:56–15:08): Chi-Chi assumes the two of them are having fun at Roshi's, then remembers the cram-school homework is only half done, and sighs. She is not worried yet.

Ep. 4, at home (22:43–23:17): she is humming, holding a returned test paper, pleased that eight hours of study a day paid off, and saying she wishes the two of them would come home so she could show it to Goku.
In the anime Piccolo arrives hovering above Kame House; in the manga he had been hidden around the corner of it, listening.
The Special Beam Cannon reads 1,330 in ep. 4 (spoken, 17:13) and 1,480 for the final shot in ep. 5 (spoken, 10:26). Both are spoken; the 1,485 in the episode page is wrong (R-20).
Dub dialogue for the rules scene: Goku says Chi-Chi is overprotective, makes Gohan study all the time, and calls martial arts a waste of energy.
Dub monologue, ep. 5: 'Goku should've been home by now… It's not good for Gohan to be away from his studies this long… He deserves to have a little fun once in a while.'

The mountain thread: ep. 3 the half-done homework · ep. 4 the returned test and the eight hours · ep. 5 the Ox-King arriving with presents · ep. 6 the phone call that reaches an answering machine. She is at home in all four and knows nothing yet.

**The telling does not happen in ep. 6.** Roshi orders Krillin to go, Bulma says the mother will kill him, and the phone gets the Kame House answering machine (14:48–15:31). **It does not happen in ep. 7 either** — Krillin gets as far as her gate, bottles it, and lies (C120).

Daizenshuu 7 places Raditz's arrival at 12 October, Age 761; the 23rd Budōkai on 7 May 756; Gohan's birth in May 757; Vegeta and Nappa on 3 November 762. Kanzenshuu notes the dates were assigned backwards from later anchors.

A Great Ape is reported as multiplying the Saiyan’s battle power by ten (C131). A tail and sufficient moonlight are relevant conditions; later pod-projected and artificial moons are possible substitutes for the natural full moon (C148). Do not imply the natural moon is the only route.

A secondary episode comparison reports that the Makankōsappō reading is anime-only. The local Japanese episode-5 caption says 1,480; the former alternative secondary figure is withdrawn (C062, R-20). The manga comparison remains separately sourced.

facts.statement: **He cannot achieve Super Saiyan God as a form.** The ritual, performed on him, does not hand him a transformation — it promotes his **baseline**: his base becomes Super Saiyan God, permanently, with no time limit and no way down. Ruled by the author.

facts.statement: Super Saiyan 1, 2 and 3 are **perfected** and therefore not forms he enters: they are internal, instant, and never announced. No hair beat, no lightning, no counting. The power is simply present.

facts.statement: A later authored Super Saiyan Rage is his signature transformation, using canon vocabulary but an original cold-anger mechanism. It remains locked in the current era. The separate 1,500 Chapter Six surge is ordinary-ki anger, not an early Super Saiyan transformation (O089).

facts.statement: **Super Saiyan 4 is his physical apex**, earned on the **ape road** — tail kept, full moon, and mastery of the Golden Ape — not by *Daima*'s gift of magic. facts.statement: Super Saiyan Blue is excluded for Goshin by the serial’s authored structural rationale: his perfected first form is internal and his later adapted godly base is permanent. This is a character-specific creative rule, not evidence that all canonical Blue users are mortal borrowers of god ki. His later god rungs remain separately authored (O038).
facts.source: author ruling — STATUS §13

facts.statement: After the crossing, **Super Saiyan God is not a form he takes: it is his base** — what he is at rest. The physical apex (Super Saiyan 4) is earned first, the crossing comes late, and Super Saiyan 4 over a divine base is the last rung.
facts.source: author ruling — STATUS §13

facts.statement: **God 1, God 2 and God 3 are conversions, not inventions.** His base is Super Saiyan God, so when he reaches for Super Saiyan 1, 2 or 3 the divine base is folded into the reaching and the divine rung is what arrives — same degree, same three gears, different substrate. **Each rung leaks**, so the climb makes him louder. God 1/2/3 is *like* Super Saiyan 1/2/3 the way a translation is like the page it came from.
facts.source: author ruling — STATUS §13

facts.statement: **The ultimate: Super Saiyan God worn inside the Super Saiyan 4 body.** The fusion of his two roads, in canon's Ultra class and not canon's (UI and UE stay other people's). Its character is the two states he already owns: **instinct when he is calm** (the body answers before he decides), **ego when he is not** (cold rage feeding on damage). **Leakage stops — fur is a vessel — so the crown is quieter than the rung below it**, and slower to arrive, because the body must accept it first.
facts.source: author ruling — STATUS §13

facts.statement: The cost rule of the whole ladder: **power up his own god rungs and he gets louder; reach the crown and he goes silent.** He never announces a rung and the narrator never numbers one.
facts.source: author ruling — STATUS §13

facts.statement: The Talent retains what has genuinely been learned or adapted; holding back, fatigue, injury or distraction can temporarily impair use or lower a reading without forgetting the skill. Preserve the separately ruled future divine promotion and conversions (STATUS §§12–14).

facts.statement: Canon describes Super Saiyan God as **cooling its user** — a calm mind, steadier ki control, described as one of the form's benefits. One encyclopaedic group (C117's source).

facts.statement: **The Talent itself becomes divine and works on everything.** After the crossing his ki, his forms, his techniques and anything he learns afterwards run on **divine qi** — the substrate is what he learns on, so nothing he acquires is ever ordinary again.
facts.source: author ruling — STATUS §14

facts.statement: **Godhood takes nothing from him.** Canon's form cools a Saiyan (C119); his promotion does not, because the retention law removes nothing (O041). He keeps his temper, appetite, jokes, grudges, grief, mistakes and attachments. **Any scene where godhood makes him serene or distant is a scene to cut.**
facts.source: author ruling — STATUS §14

facts.statement: **His children are born divine, not mortal.** The line does not begin at a ritual; it begins at him. Ruled; the children themselves are unwritten (OPEN-11).
facts.source: author ruling — STATUS §14

facts.statement: At four and through the Z-era arcs Goshin is mortal, with ordinary ki, flight and techniques; no golden transformation, god ki or divine form. The separately ruled ladder is for a later era. Mortal does not mean static, incapable or unable to grow.

facts.statement: FORM: EPISODE remains the default for new chapters, with anime grammar and the form-aware 4,400–6,600 word band. Chapters One and Two retain legacy scene length after authorized targeted revisions; a complete episode-form rebuild is not implied. Chapter Three uses the title and schooling reference Eight Hours without a literal countdown. Camera movement does not confer canon-character interiority.

facts.statement: A fight is clear in geography, participants, actions, stakes and consequences. Flight, named techniques, multiple supernatural actions and sourced or authored readings are allowed. Damage follows feats, attack, aim and conditions, not a fixed formula (WRITING §§11,16).
facts.source: author ruling — fights and the supernatural are the weakest writing

facts.statement: Write supernatural action directly and coherently: cause, movement, effect, consequence. Do not compare it to ordinary furniture, flag it as impossible or report what could not be seen. Multiple supernatural actions and visible ordinary ki are allowed; no early god ki (WRITING §12).
facts.source: author ruling — fights and the supernatural are the weakest writing

facts.statement: CRAFT.md has three authored specimens: controlled spar, hillside blast and flight/technique practice. They are exercises, not canonical beats.

facts.statement: **Once a character is named on the page, the narration calls them by that name.** No epithets for named characters — not 'the taller boy', not 'the small one', not 'the demon', not 'the woman with blue hair'. **Three legal exceptions only:** before the name is known (once), for a character who is never named (declared as furniture), and inside dialogue. **Gated by `check_names`.**
facts.source: author ruling — epithets read as withholding

facts.topic: craft — the crib, and the clarity law
facts.statement: **A fight must be followable in one pass** (`WRITING §11 law 0`): every paragraph answers *where are they · who is acting · what changed*. **One action per sentence; no pronoun with two possible owners.** Effect-only prose is a mood, not a sequence. **Every specimen carries a plain-words crib first** — numbered, adjective-free — because if the crib is unclear the prose is broken, not the reader.
facts.source: author ruling — the fight could not be followed

facts.topic: craft — no riddles in invented material
facts.statement: Invented material must be plain and understandable without prior scenes. Characters do not speak in aphorisms or announce facts already shown: the authority orders and the learner acts. Context and action make the stake clear; every craft specimen begins with WHAT THIS IS and a plain-words crib.
facts.source: author ruling — the invented prose reads as a riddle

facts.statement: **The impossible runs on flow** (`WRITING §15`). **Never tell the reader they could not see it** — *no 'nobody saw', no 'blink of an eye'*; write the displacement and let the ground report it. **Never compare the impossible to something ordinary** — no doors, pages, bowls, fists. **Never stop to say it is strange** — the reader knows. Shape: **cause you can point at → event → consequence left in the world**, no gaps. **And a character may not announce what the scene already shows:** no *'he has a tail'* — let the one with authority give the order and the boy act.
facts.source: author ruling — the supernatural comparisons and the announcements read wrong

facts.statement: A fight declares its participants, condition, relevant demonstrated capabilities, attack and environment. Damage follows the scene and feats, not a numerical battle-power conversion. Bodies are not categorically small-damage and large feats need not always require a long charge (WRITING §16).

facts.statement: At 14:59–18:14 Gohan repeatedly awakens the robot about a scorpion and hunger. It first tells him to stop; eventually it directs him to find food in the cave. Gohan asks it to cook and asks for a mother-style flavor; it tells him how to use its head and oven and he says the food tastes bad. facts.topic: episode 9 animal pursuit, ravine and food — secondary reports
facts.statement: W-69 reports an alligator, sabretooth, eagle and flying reptile preceding the desert fall, a steep ravine at the exit, and mushrooms cooked for Gohan. W-70 instead describes Gohan grabbing the large bird’s leg, while W-69 says the bird seizes Gohan; neither account is verified footage. W-67 and W-68 summarize the hole and buried robot. The local captions explicitly label a sabretooth growl and eagle call, but do not establish the full visual choreography or the named food.

facts.statement: At 18:20–19:29 the robot says an excavation accident and unstable ground buried it in the ruins about eighty years earlier. Gohan recognizes the Nemurian temple from a book and wants to free the robot. The robot says it intends to save energy and emerge on its own, objects to being disturbed and warns that Gohan’s digging will upset the balance.

facts.topic: episode 9 collapse, wires and energy gas
facts.statement: At 19:32–24:17 the robot warns that the cave is collapsing, urges Gohan to leave, asks him to join blue and red wires in its head, calls for full power and tells him to go. Later it says it has used up its energy gas, urges him on, and becomes unresponsive as he calls to it. W-67 and W-69 describe it saving Gohan and being left behind; silent rescue choreography and any permanent-death diagnosis are not established by captions alone.

In the separate 25:57–26:22 preview Gohan asks about Tien and Yamcha and Goku wonders whether they know of his death. This is a preview, not evidence that either fighter meets anyone during episode 9. facts.statement: W-70 reports that dead Goku runs along Snake Way, wonders if he can eat a cloud and is later shown having eaten it. facts.topic: chapter ten — examination, food and journey
facts.statement: The doctor re-examines Goshin the morning after Chapter Nine and permits a gentle monitored passenger trip, not independent flight, running, heavy lifting or training; he must rest and report symptoms and needs another follow-up. The family visits Korin and Kami, stops to check him and returns home before late. He watches the raw food, cooking, packing, reheating and lemon preparation before the portions he eats; he does not eat a Senzu. Goku and Gohan remain fully healed and restored.

facts.topic: chapter ten — family safety, moon and Kami warning
facts.statement: Chi-Chi and Goku choose to keep the family together on the journey, acknowledge Piccolo may find them and reject any guarantee of safety. Kami says his life is tied to Piccolo and shares his uncertain approximately one-year feeling, not a certain death date or wish. Goku tells Kami the moon warning; the family keeps its precautions. Yemma has granted no passage, Baba has given no answer, and Goku has not agreed to leave for King Kai. Goku temporarily goes to the desert only after the family explicitly weighs separation while Kami, Popo, Chi-Chi, Ox-King and Yajirobe remain with the boys.

facts.topic: chapter ten — Gohan’s book and survey contact
facts.statement: Gohan and Goshin examine a machine book; Gohan asks about the Nemurian site and Popo tunes a regional survey bulletin about an unstable desert excavation. Goku volunteers, demonstrates controlled lifting and works under the survey crew’s directions. By radio Gohan identifies the likely SSS type, Goshin answers Goku after an explicit invitation and identifies the orientation of the old exit; Goshin remains at the lookout under his medical limits. The workers, bulletin and radio are authored, not episode footage.

facts.topic: chapter ten — C-6’s consent and damaged sensor
facts.statement: Goku activates buried C-6; the robot asks for sleep, accepts one question and then asks about a supported rescue. C-6 recounts about eighty years trapped, warns that digging can bring down the roof and agrees to an attempt after considering the plan. Goku clears loose sand only with permission; the sensor remains cracked and works imperfectly. The altered initial encounter and consent are branch staging.

facts.topic: chapter ten — tremor, extraction and uncertain recovery
facts.statement: An independent new tremor destabilizes the site; Goku holds a slab while C-6 agrees to a red-and-blue emergency connection, uses remaining energy to move and is carried out. This authored rescue and its different outcome depend on additional help. C-6 is responsive afterward but nearly out of energy, declines unauthorized reconnection and elects to be switched off. It is unknown whether he can wake; no refill or completed repair is asserted.

facts.topic: chapter ten — robot at lookout and remaining threads
facts.statement: Popo agrees to keep C-6 quiet at the lookout; the survey office and possibly Bulma may be contacted, but no specialist has examined him yet. A little lemon is prepared in Goshin’s view for C-6’s suggested seasoning, which tastes too sour. The family returns to the mountain house with the Four-Star Ball on Gohan’s hat; the Three- and Six-Star Balls remain in the home cupboard, and no wish or tail change occurs. Krillin’s fighter search and the promised Chapter Eleven preview remain future work.
